name: Russia–NATO
value: Russian drone over Poland; no Article 4
summary: Poland says on 24 Nov a Russian drone deliberately entered its airspace; NATO weighs extra forces; no Article 4 request
state: Poland's deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski said on 24 Nov that a Russian attack-capable drone briefly entered Polish airspace and that Warsaw assumes it was deliberate; forces tracked it but chose not to shoot it down to avoid civilian harm (European Pravda). NATO said on 23 Nov its top commander was considering extra forces for the region, after Russian missile debris was found at sites in eastern Poland on 20 Nov. Estonia plans to close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 Dec (AP). No Article 4 request or direct clash was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Residents of eastern Poland and the Baltic states should follow local civil-defence alerts. Travellers to Estonia should check FCDO advice, as land crossings to Russia are due to close from 1 Dec.
rubric_hit: Watch: airspace violation — Russian drone in Polish airspace, judged deliberate by Poland's defence ministry on 24 Nov; no Article 4 or clash

sources.title: European Pravda — Polish Defence Ministry believes Russia deliberately sent drone into Polish airspace

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
